price_note: Prices tax-included, from the shop's own Gnavi official page (gexc200.gorp.jp → r.gnavi.co.jp/0001033061/menu1). A user-logged Tabelog card from 2018 shows the same two sizes at ¥3,500 / ¥4,800, so the Gnavi figures are the newer ones. The shop's own page carries a stale ¥4,800 photo caption alongside the ¥4,900 table entry — take ¥4,900. Prices approximate — may change. Founded 1861; no reservations, cash, lunch only 11:30–14:00, closes when the eel runs out.

items.en: Charcoal-grilled eel over rice in a lacquered box, standard portion, with pickles and clear soup. The eel is steamed then grilled Tokyo-style, so it is soft rather than crisp, and painted repeatedly with a tare kept alive since 1861
items.note: 蒲焼のタレは醤油・味醂ベース＝小麦。The glaze is wheat soy sauce brushed on through the grilling; there is no gluten-free version. The 吸物 clear soup is also soy-seasoned.

items.en: The same box with a noticeably larger helping of eel — what most regulars order
items.note: 同じ醤油ベースのタレ＝小麦。Same wheat-soy tare.

items.en: Kabayaki — the glazed grilled eel served on its own, without the rice box, for eating with sake
items.note: 蒲焼＝醤油ダレ＝小麦。Wheat soy in the glaze.

items.en: Shirayaki — eel grilled plain with no glaze at all, eaten with wasabi and salt, or soy on the side. The way to taste the fish rather than the sauce
items.note: 白焼き自体は無味付けだが、つけ醤油は通常の小麦醤油。刷毛やグリルは蒲焼と共用。The eel itself is unglazed, which makes this the only possible route to eel here for a wheat avoider — but the dipping soy served alongside is ordinary wheat shoyu, so ask for salt and wasabi only. The grill is shared with the tare-painted kabayaki.

items.en: Boxes are available to take away — useful given the queue and the twelve seats
items.note: 同じ蒲焼＝小麦醤油。Same wheat-soy product. Listed on the shop's Gnavi page; no separate price published.
